working: Coplanarity/intersection: det[(3-1, k-(-1), 0-1); (2,3,4); (1,2,1)] = det[(2,k+1,-1);(2,3,4);(1,2,1)] = 2(3-8) - (k+1)(2-4) - 1(4-3) = 2k - 9 = 0, so k = 9/2. Verified by actual solve: s = -3/2, t = -5 gives the common point (-2,-5.5,-5) on both lines.

Points (1,3,1), (0,1,2); directions (1,-lambda,lambda) and (1/2,1,-1). Coplanar: det[(-1,-2,1);(1,-lambda,lambda);(1/2,1,-1)] = -(lambda-lambda) + 2(-1-lambda/2) + (1+lambda/2) = -1 - lambda/2 = 0, so lambda = -2.
xy-plane is z = 0. Section formula: z = (6m + 4n)/(m+n) = 0 gives 6m = -4n, m:n = -2:3. A negative ratio means external division in the ratio 2:3.

Intercept form x/a + y/b + z/c = 1 cuts axes at (a,0,0),(0,b,0),(0,0,c); centroid = (a/3, b/3, c/3) = (alpha,beta,gamma), so a = 3alpha etc. Plane becomes x/(3alpha)+y/(3beta)+z/(3gamma)=1, i.e. x/alpha + y/beta + z/gamma = 3.
notes: OCR damage in options (A) and (C): both print '\alpha\alpha' where the intended term is 'alpha*x'. Does not affect the answer, which is (D).

working: V = |det[(1,a,1);(0,1,a);(a,0,1)]| = |1 + a^3 - a|. Minimising f(a) = a^3 - a + 1 gives f'(a) = 3a^2 - 1 = 0, a = 1/sqrt(3) (the local minimum; a = -1/sqrt(3) is the local maximum).
notes: Strictly, |a^3-a+1| attains its true global minimum of 0 at the real root a = -1.3247..., which is in no option. The question intends the stationary point of the unsigned cubic, giving 1/sqrt(3) = (C).

working: Coefficient matrix in the basis (a,b,c) is upper triangular: rows (1,2,3), (0,lambda,4), (0,0,2lambda-1). det = lambda(2lambda-1), non-zero unless lambda = 0 or lambda = 1/2 - so non-coplanar for all except two values.

(a x b) x c = (a.c)b - (b.c)a. Matching with (1/3)|b||c|a forces a.c = 0 and -(b.c) = (1/3)|b||c|, i.e. cos(angle b,c) = -1/3. The ACUTE angle theta therefore has cos theta = 1/3, so sin theta = sqrt(1-1/9) = 2sqrt(2)/3.
notes: Stem OCR: '(1/3)|b \parallel c|a' is the mangled form of (1/3)|b||c|a - readable. Also the Passage I text for Q9-Q10 is spliced onto the end of option (D).

working: Coplanarity det[(-1,1,1);(2,3,lambda);(3,2,3)] = 5lambda - 20 = 0, so lambda = 4. Solving the two lines: s = t = 1 gives the intersection (5,5,5). Checking options, only x = y = z holds (3x+y+z=25 not 20; 2x+y+z=20 not 25; 3x+2y+z=30 not 24).

With lambda = 4, normal of the common plane = (2,3,4) x (3,2,3) = (1,6,-5); plane is x + 6y - 5z = 10. Dot with the normal (4,1,2) of 4x+y+2z=0 gives 4 + 6 - 10 = 0, so the normals - and hence the planes - are perpendicular: pi/2.

working: 1 + omega = -omega^2, so (1+omega)^7 = (-omega^2)^7 = -omega^14 = -omega^2 = 1 + omega. Hence A + B*omega = 1 + omega, (A,B) = (1,1).
Two DISTINCT roots on Re(z)=1 cannot both be real (they would both equal 1), so they are conjugates 1 +/- it with t non-zero. Then beta = product = 1 + t^2 > 1, so beta is in (1, infinity).

working: All of (1,1),(2,2),(3,3) present so reflexive. (1,2) is in R but (2,1) is not, so not symmetric. Transitivity holds: (1,2)&(2,3) gives (1,3) which is present, and every other chain is already in R. So reflexive but not symmetric.

|z| = 1 so conj(z) = 1/z, giving 1 + conj(z) = (z+1)/z. Hence (1+z)/(1+conj(z)) = z, whose argument is theta.
arg(sqrt3+i) = pi/6, arg(1-i*sqrt3) = -pi/3. arg z = (4n+1)(pi/6) - 4n(-pi/3) = (4n+1)pi/6 + 8n*pi/6 = (12n+1)pi/6 = 2n*pi + pi/6, so the argument is pi/6.

Substituting x = -1/y into x^2+5x+2=0 gives 1/y^2 - 5/y + 2 = 0, i.e. 2y^2 - 5y + 1 = 0 - the first equation. So each root of the second is the negative reciprocal of a root of the first. Numerically: roots 0.2192, 2.2808 and -4.5616, -0.4384. Products 1/2 and 2 differ, ruling out (C).
